name: Foel Wen Hut: self-run practice weekend (group booking, up to 6)
summary: Stone hut for up to 6 experienced practitioners to run their own weekend of long sitting. No teacher. Silence except at the shared evening meal. £40.
description:
Foel Wen is a two-room stone hut at 400m in the Berwyn range, maintained by our sangha since 1986. There is no teacher and no programme. The hut is available for self-run practice weekends.

**Booking**
Group bookings for two to six practitioners who already sit and want a weekend of extended practice alongside others, without anyone organising it. The group arranges its own schedule on arrival.

**Practice**
Practitioners set their own schedule. A typical weekend is five or six sitting periods of 45 to 60 minutes daily, with walking between, beginning early. The hut has cushions, benches, a wood stove, and a bell.

**Silence**
Silence from waking until the evening meal. The evening meal is the exception: the group cooks and eats together and may talk. Silence resumes after.

**Requirements**
This is a demanding weekend: long sitting, a cold hut in the mornings, a steep hill, and nobody to moderate the schedule. We ask that every member of the group has an established daily practice and has completed at least one residential retreat. We do not verify this. The hut is not the place to discover you were not ready.

**Keyholder**
Pauline lives at the farm below and holds the key. She brings bread on Saturday and otherwise leaves the group alone.

**Cost**
£40 per person per weekend, to the sangha, for wood and upkeep.
practical: Friday evening to Sunday afternoon, most weekends. £40 per person. Sleeps 6 on platforms; bring sleeping bags and mats. Cold water, wood stove, composting toilet, no electricity. Bring all food except bread; nearest shop 9 miles. Park at the farm, 20-minute walk up. No mobile signal.
